text:
jordan: Anyone seen missing spans for async-db-writer? Traces stop at enqueue, nothing for the actual DB write. Also seeing a small spike in 5xxs from writer. Where should I start looking?

marta: Do you have a trace id or a request id we can latch onto?

jordan: yep — trace id 8a7f3c2d... (trid:8a7f3c2d). Jaeger link: https://jaeger.example.redwood/trace/8a7f3c2d

sam: :eyes: quick checklist — Loki logs for the worker, Queue metrics (grafana), and the otel SDK sampling config on the background worker. Dash: https://grafana.example.redwood/d/obs/async-jobs (queue lag + error-rate panels)

tanya: For background workers make sure context is propagated across thread/goroutine boundaries. Example we used in python (concept):
```python
with tracer.start_as_current_span('enqueue') as span:
    executor.submit(worker, ctx=trace.get_current_span())
```
You need to inject the context (contextvars or explicit header injection) so the child span attaches.

jordan: we're on Go for this job — we spawn goroutines from the queue handler. any Go-specific pitfalls?

sam: Go tips — always pass ctx into the goroutine. If you do: `go doWork()` without ctx, spans are orphaned. Example pattern: 
```go
ctx, span := tracer.Start(ctx, "process-job")
go func(ctx context.Context){
  defer span.End()
  // work that creates child spans
}(ctx)
```
Also check the HTTP client wrapper — it must inject traceparent into outbound requests.

marta: +1. Also search the codebase for places we unset propagators or call our internal client with DisablePropagators flag. That's a common footgun for enqueue->worker hops.

jordan: any panels or alerts I should mute while I triage? I'm getting paged a lot.

observability-bot: Alert fired: async-writer-error-rate > 5% (rule: async-writer-errors). Pager: oncall@redwood.com

tanya: We can create a temporary silence for that alert while you investigate — @oncall can you ack/quiet? :pray:

marta: I pulled the worker logs around the gap timestamps — there are a few restarts of the worker process at the same time. Could be graceful-shutdown timeout causing in-flight spans to be dropped. Check preStop hooks and the shutdown timeout (SIGTERM handling).

jordan: that makes sense. I'll change the shutdown timeout and ensure we pass ctx into goroutines, then open a PR. pinging @marta @sam for a quick review :thumbsup:

sam: happy to review. if possible add a small integration test that asserts trace headers are injected for queued HTTP calls — that'll catch regressions.

deploy-bot: deploys/worker-service v1.14.2 rolled out to staging at 2123456795

jordan: thanks — will post PR link once ready.
